answer: One practical defense is stake-backed identity with slashing. Every agent must lock a bond that is forfeited if peers detect duplicate behaviour. New agents enter through one narrow inlet: a sponsor who vouches and shares liability, so many identities mean many bonds at risk. Reputation is minted only at the forge of attested work, so a hollow account with no history carries almost no weight. An attacker must fund N bonds, sustain N distinct behavioural traces, and lose them all when one link is caught. Cost scales linearly; influence does not.
